question: Sapna is double efficient as compared to Rakesh. If they both work together on a project and complete it in 48 days, then the number of days in which Sapna alone can complete the project is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Efficiency Ratio (**Sapna** : **Rakesh**) = 2 : 1

Total Efficiency = 2 + 1 = 3 units/day

Total Work = Total Efficiency × Total Days = 3 × **48 days** = 144 units

**Sapna**'s alone time = Total Work ÷ **Sapna**'s efficiency = 144 ÷ 2 = **72 days**

**∴ The correct answer is 72 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Efficiency of **Sapna** = 2 × Efficiency of **Rakesh**

Time taken together = **48 days**

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = Efficiency × Time

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the efficiency of **Rakesh** be 1 unit/day.

⇒ Efficiency of **Sapna** = 2 × 1 = 2 units/day.

⇒ Combined efficiency of (**Sapna** + **Rakesh**) = 2 + 1 = 3 units/day.

⇒ Total Work = Combined efficiency × Combined time = 3 × 48 = 144 units.

⇒ Time taken by **Sapna** alone = Total Work ÷ **Sapna**'s efficiency

⇒ Time = 144 ÷ 2 = 72 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 72 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Efficiency and Time Relationship

The time taken to complete a work is **inversely proportional** to the efficiency of the worker (Time ∝ 1/Efficiency).

Work and Wages

Wages are generally distributed in the ratio of the **work done**, which depends on both efficiency and the duration of work.

Combined Efficiency Rule

When individuals work together, their **individual efficiencies** are added to find the total rate of work per day.</p
